endometriosis.name: Endometriosis
endometriosis.scope: Pelvic endometriosis, deep infiltrating endometriosis, endometrioma (chocolate cyst), uterosacral nodularity, cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, laparoscopy, medical management
endometriosis.core: Reproductive-age patient with progressive cyclic pelvic pain, deep dyspareunia, and infertility from ectopic endometrial tissue.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Early menarche, short cycles, prolonged menstruation, family history; obstructed menstrual outflow

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Uterosacral nodularity**, fixed retroverted uterus, posterior cul-de-sac tenderness
Dyschezia or cyclic rectal bleeding → bowel involvement; urinary cyclic symptoms → bladder disease
Pain severity poorly correlates with lesion burden; examination may be normal

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Estrogen-responsive implants provoke inflammation, fibrosis, adhesions, and distortion of pelvic anatomy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical assessment + **transvaginal ultrasound** first; normal imaging cannot exclude superficial disease
MRI maps deep lesions or indeterminate adnexal masses; CA-125 not a diagnostic test
★ **Laparoscopy with biopsy** for uncertain diagnosis, refractory symptoms, or planned operative treatment
Current ACOG approach supports presumptive clinical diagnosis; surgery not required before empiric treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pain, no immediate pregnancy goal → **NSAID + continuous combined OCP** or progestin
Persistent symptoms → GnRH agonist/antagonist with add-back hormones to limit hypoestrogenic adverse effects
Refractory disease or selected infertility → laparoscopic excision/ablation and adhesiolysis
Endometrioma surgery may reduce ovarian reserve; balance pain, suspicion, size, and fertility goals
Trying to conceive → fertility evaluation; hormonal suppression does not improve spontaneous conception

rows.label: Complications
items: Adhesive infertility, bowel/ureteral obstruction, chronic pain; small increase in clear-cell/endometrioid ovarian cancer
GnRH suppression → hot flashes, bone loss; disease may recur after conservative surgery

rows.label: Prevention
items: Postoperative hormonal suppression reduces pain recurrence when pregnancy not desired; no established primary prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Adenomyosis: diffusely enlarged, boggy uterus with heavy bleeding
PID: fever, discharge, cervical motion tenderness; pain less cyclic
Primary dysmenorrhea: normal examination, onset soon after menarche, no structural lesion

table.title: Anatomic forms
rows: Fibrotic nodules involving ligaments, bowel, bladder
Ovarian chocolate cyst; homogeneous ground-glass ultrasound echoes

gestational-diabetes-mellitus.name: Gestational diabetes mellitus
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Screening (50g oral glucose challenge at 24-28 weeks), diagnostic 3-hour 100g test, glycemic targets, nutritional therapy, insulin, fetal and neonatal complications (macrosomia, hypoglycemia, RDS, polycythemia)
gestational-diabetes-mellitus.core: Pregnancy-induced insulin resistance unmasks hyperglycemia, increasing fetal insulin secretion and growth; screen routinely at 24–28 weeks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Obesity, prior GDM/macrosomia, family history of type 2 diabetes, PCOS
High-risk patients need early assessment for previously unrecognized overt diabetes

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; excessive fetal growth or polyhydramnios may prompt evaluation
Early marked hyperglycemia suggests preexisting diabetes rather than typical later-onset GDM

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Placental hormones increase maternal insulin requirements; inadequate beta-cell compensation causes dysglycemia
Maternal glucose crosses placenta; insulin does not; fetal hyperinsulinemia persists briefly after birth

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Two-step screen: **nonfasting 50 g challenge**, 1-hour threshold 130–140 mg/dL by local protocol
Positive challenge → fasting 100 g, 3-hour OGTT; **≥2 abnormal values** diagnose GDM
Alternative one-step 75 g OGTT: fasting ≥92, 1-hour ≥180, or 2-hour ≥153 mg/dL
HbA1c alone does not replace pregnancy glucose testing

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First: **individualized nutrition, activity, home glucose monitoring**; avoid severe carbohydrate restriction
★ Targets: fasting **<95**, 1-hour <140, or 2-hour <120 mg/dL
Above targets despite lifestyle → **insulin preferred**; metformin crosses placenta, counsel if used
Medication need or poor control → fetal surveillance; delivery timing depends on control and obstetric findings
Suspected fetal weight ≥4,500 g with diabetes → discuss planned cesarean

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal: preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, future type 2 diabetes
Fetal: macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, birth trauma; poor control increases stillbirth risk
Neonate: **hypoglycemia**, RDS, polycythemia, jaundice; congenital anomalies mainly reflect pregestational diabetes

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Postpartum **75 g OGTT at 4–12 weeks**; lifelong diabetes testing every 1–3 years
Breastfeeding, weight management, activity; most GDM insulin needs resolve after placental delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pregestational diabetes: overt diagnostic-range hyperglycemia early in pregnancy
Physiologic glycosuria: lower renal threshold without diagnostic blood glucose abnormalities

hirsutism.name: Hirsutism
hirsutism.scope: Idiopathic hirsutism, peripheral 5-alpha-reductase overactivity, evaluation of androgen excess, nonclassic CAH, androgen-secreting neoplasms, oral contraceptives, spironolactone
hirsutism.core: Terminal hair in androgen-dependent areas in women requires distinguishing gradual androgen sensitivity/PCOS from rapid virilization due to a secreting tumor.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: PCOS, familial/ethnic hair distribution, nonclassic CAH, exogenous androgens/anabolic steroids
Rare ovarian/adrenal neoplasm; medications causing generalized hypertrichosis differ from androgenic hair growth

rows.label: Clues
items: Facial, chest, lower-abdominal terminal hair; acne and irregular menses favor androgen excess
★ **Rapid progression, deep voice, clitoromegaly**, increased muscle mass → tumor evaluation
Regular ovulatory cycles with normal androgens and slow growth favor idiopathic hirsutism

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Androgens convert vellus to terminal hairs; follicular 5-alpha-reductase converts testosterone to potent DHT
Idiopathic disease reflects increased peripheral sensitivity despite normal circulating hormones

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Moderate/severe hair growth or endocrine signs → morning **total testosterone**, reliable assay
DHEA-S assesses adrenal source; early-morning follicular **17-hydroxyprogesterone** screens nonclassic CAH
Marked testosterone elevation, often >150–200 ng/dL → pelvic imaging; DHEA-S >700 µg/dL → adrenal imaging
Equivocal 17-hydroxyprogesterone → ACTH stimulation; TSH/prolactin or cortisol testing only for matching features
Mild localized hair without abnormal cycles/endocrine signs often needs no extensive hormone workup

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pregnancy not desired → **combined OCP** first-line; reassess after ≥6 months
★ Persistent symptoms → add **spironolactone with reliable contraception**; monitor potassium/renal function
Shaving, waxing, laser/photoepilation; topical eflornithine slows facial hair growth
Treat tumor/endocrine cause; weight loss benefits metabolic risk and androgen excess in PCOS

rows.label: Complications
items: Psychological distress; spironolactone → hyperkalemia, menstrual irregularity, male fetal undervirilization
Estrogen contraception → VTE risk; avoid when estrogen contraindicated

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid androgen supplements; counsel slow hair-cycle response and ongoing maintenance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypertrichosis: diffuse nonandrogen distribution; minoxidil, phenytoin, cyclosporine
Cushing syndrome: striae, proximal weakness, easy bruising accompany hair changes

hirsutism.evidence: Treatment checked 2026-10-30: [SOGC 444](https://www.sogc.org/common/Uploaded%20files/ACSC/ACSC2024/gui444CPG2312E.pdf); biochemical localization established endocrine teaching.

hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.name: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.scope: Chronic and gestational HTN, preeclampsia, HELLP, eclampsia
hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy.core: Pregnancy-associated hypertension; maternal organ injury or placental dysfunction signals danger even without substantial proteinuria.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior preeclampsia, chronic HTN, CKD, diabetes, SLE/APS, multifetal gestation
Nulliparity, obesity, age ≥35, family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Headache, visual disturbance, RUQ/epigastric pain, dyspnea; edema nonspecific
★ Severe features: **platelets <100,000/µL**, creatinine >1.1 mg/dL or doubled, transaminases ≥2× normal
Other severe features: pulmonary edema, refractory neurologic symptoms
Presentation through **6 weeks postpartum**; eclampsia/HELLP possible without prior HTN

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Abnormal spiral-artery remodeling → placental ischemia → systemic endothelial injury, vasospasm, capillary leak

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **BP ≥140/90**, either component, twice ≥4 h apart; severe ≥160/110 confirmed within minutes
CBC/platelets, creatinine, AST/ALT, urine protein; fetal growth US + antenatal testing
Proteinuria: **≥300 mg/24 h** or protein/creatinine ≥0.3; dipstick 2+ only if quantification unavailable
Chronic HTN + new proteinuria/end-organ injury → superimposed preeclampsia; HELLP: smear, LDH ≥600 IU/L

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Persistent severe BP ≥15 min → **IV labetalol/hydralazine** or immediate-release oral nifedipine within 30–60 min
★ Severe preeclampsia/eclampsia → **magnesium sulfate** through 24 h postpartum; airway before delivery
Chronic HTN ≥140/90 → oral labetalol/extended-release nifedipine; avoid ACE inhibitors/ARBs
Mg toxicity: areflexia/hypoventilation → stop infusion, **IV calcium gluconate**; oliguria → reduce dose

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, abruption, DIC, AKI, hepatic hematoma/rupture; fetal growth restriction, prematurity, death

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ High risk or multiple moderate risks → **aspirin 81 mg/day**, start 12–28 wk, ideally before 16
Postpartum BP review within 72 h if severe, otherwise 7–10 days; long-term cardiovascular follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: TTP: profound thrombocytopenia/hemolysis, persists after delivery
Acute fatty liver: hypoglycemia, jaundice, marked coagulopathy
Epilepsy: established seizure disorder; evaluate alternative causes despite obstetric context

table.title: Classification and delivery
rows: Before 20 wk or persists >12 wk postpartum
After 20 wk + proteinuria OR severe features
Severe BP alone sufficient; <34 stable → betamethasone
Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets
Deliver after stabilization, any gestational age

infertility.name: Infertility
infertility.scope: Definition (failure to conceive after 12 months), initial evaluation, semen analysis (male factor), ovulatory status (midluteal progesterone), tubal and uterine factors (hysterosalpingography), ovarian reserve testing
infertility.core: No conception after 12 months of regular unprotected intercourse; evaluate after 6 months at age ≥35, immediately over 40 or with risks.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, PCOS, endometriosis, PID, pelvic surgery, chemotherapy, testicular injury, exogenous testosterone
Smoking, marked weight extremes, premature ovarian insufficiency, untreated endocrine disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Irregular/absent cycles → ovulatory dysfunction; galactorrhea → hyperprolactinemia; hot flashes → ovarian insufficiency
Prior ectopic pregnancy or chlamydia → tubal damage; normal cycles do not exclude male factor

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Failure of sperm production/delivery, oocyte release, fertilization, transport, or implantation; mixed factors common

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Evaluate **both partners simultaneously**; reproductive history, sexual timing, examinations; semen analysis early
Abnormal semen result → repeat and male reproductive evaluation; do not begin with female laparoscopy
★ Ovulation uncertain → **progesterone about 7 days before expected menses**; >3 ng/mL supports ovulation
Regular 21–35-day cycles usually imply ovulation; targeted TSH, prolactin only for relevant symptoms
★ **HSG** for tubal patency; saline sonography for cavity; avoid HSG during pregnancy/infection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ PCOS anovulation → **letrozole**; hyperprolactinemia → cabergoline; correct thyroid disease
Tubal occlusion/severe male factor → IVF, sometimes intracytoplasmic sperm injection
Unexplained infertility → ovarian stimulation with intrauterine insemination, then IVF if unsuccessful
Intercourse every 1–2 days during fertile window; avoid testosterone for fertility-seeking men

rows.label: Complications
items: Psychological distress; stimulation → ovarian hyperstimulation, multiple gestation; assisted reproduction → ectopic pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: STI prevention, tobacco cessation, weight optimization; fertility preservation before gonadotoxic treatment
Preconception folic acid and medication review

rows.label: Mimics
items: Infrequent intercourse: inadequate exposure despite normal reproductive testing
Recurrent pregnancy loss: conception occurs, followed by repeated losses

table.title: Ovarian reserve: treatment response, not natural fertility
rows: Low values suggest reduced follicular pool

infertility.evidence: Evaluation checked 2026-10-30: [ASRM 2021](https://www.asrm.org/practice-guidance/practice-committee-documents/fertility-evaluation-of-infertile-women-a-committee-opinion-2021/); treatment established reproductive guidance.

interstitial-cystitis.name: Interstitial cystitis
interstitial-cystitis.scope: Bladder pain syndrome, chronic pelvic pain relieved by voiding, urinary urgency and frequency, Hunner lesions on cystoscopy, dietary triggers, pentosan polysulfate, behavioral modification
interstitial-cystitis.core: Bladder-associated pain worsens with filling and improves after voiding, with urinary frequency but repeatedly negative infection testing.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: More common in women; associated chronic pelvic pain, fibromyalgia, IBS
Symptoms may flare with stress, intercourse, menstruation, acidic foods, caffeine, or alcohol

rows.label: Clues
items: Suprapubic pressure/discomfort, urgency, nocturia; often small voided volumes and dyspareunia
★ **Symptoms >6 weeks**, sterile cultures, no alternate explanation support bladder pain syndrome
Patients void to relieve discomfort rather than primarily to prevent urge incontinence
Fever, flank pain, gross hematuria, weight loss → evaluate other disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Heterogeneous urothelial dysfunction, neural sensitization, and pelvic-floor muscle abnormalities generate chronic pain
Hunner-lesion subtype includes focal inflammatory mucosal injury; absence of lesions does not exclude disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **History, pelvic examination, urinalysis/culture**; review pain/voiding diary and check residual when retention suspected
Hematuria or cancer risk → malignancy evaluation rather than presumptive diagnosis
Cystoscopy when uncertain or suspect Hunner lesions; not required for every uncomplicated presentation
Glomerulations are nonspecific; potassium sensitivity testing is not recommended

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Education, trigger elimination, bladder training, stress management**; individualized multimodal treatment
Pelvic-floor tenderness → **manual physical therapy**; avoid strengthening/Kegel exercises when hypertonic
Persistent symptoms: selected amitriptyline, cimetidine, hydroxyzine, or intravesical lidocaine/heparin
★ **Pentosan polysulfate may cause pigmentary maculopathy**; discuss limited benefit and arrange retinal monitoring
Hunner lesions → cystoscopic fulguration or triamcinolone injection; refractory severe disease → specialist interventions

rows.label: Complications
items: Sleep disruption, sexual dysfunction, anxiety/depression, substantial quality-of-life impairment
Rare advanced fibrotic low-capacity bladder; treatments may cause sedation, anticholinergic effects, or retention

rows.label: Prevention
items: Identify individual dietary triggers; avoid unnecessary repeated antibiotics with negative cultures
Plan flare management and regular reassessment; no established primary-prevention strategy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Overactive bladder: urgency/incontinence predominates without filling-related pain
UTI: positive culture; bladder cancer: hematuria, risk factors, abnormal cystoscopy
Endometriosis: cyclic pelvic pain with gynecologic features

intra-amniotic-infection.name: Intra-amniotic infection
intra-amniotic-infection.scope: Chorioamnionitis, clinical diagnostic criteria (maternal fever, fetal tachycardia, purulent fluid, uterine tenderness), IV ampicillin and gentamicin, labor augmentation, postpartum endometritis
intra-amniotic-infection.core: Intrapartum fever with fetal tachycardia or purulent cervical drainage suggests ascending infection requiring antibiotics and delivery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prolonged membrane rupture, prolonged labor, repeated digital examinations after rupture, internal monitoring
Genital tract colonization; infection can occur with intact membranes

rows.label: Clues
items: Uterine tenderness, foul amniotic fluid, maternal tachycardia, leukocytosis
Hypotension, altered mentation, oliguria → maternal sepsis; leukocytosis alone nonspecific during labor

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Polymicrobial ascent from vagina into decidua, membranes, amniotic fluid, and fetus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected infection: temperature **≥39°C**, or **38–38.9°C plus one additional clinical risk factor**
Additional factors: fetal baseline >160/min, purulent cervical drainage, maternal leukocytosis without corticosteroids
ACOG 2024 permits diagnosis without fever when other clinical findings strongly support infection
Clinical diagnosis; placental histology or amniotic-fluid testing confirms retrospectively; never delay treatment
Sepsis → blood cultures, lactate, CBC, renal function; cultures before antibiotics only without delay

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Prompt **IV ampicillin + gentamicin**, acetaminophen, IV fluids; notify neonatal team
★ Induce/augment labor with **oxytocin**; infection alone is not a cesarean indication
Cesarean for obstetric indication → add clindamycin for anaerobic coverage; postpartum dosing depends on course
Shock → fluid resuscitation, norepinephrine, urgent source control; do not await fetal lung maturity

rows.label: Complications
items: Uterine atony/hemorrhage, postpartum endometritis, bacteremia, septic shock
Neonatal pneumonia, sepsis, meningitis; prematurity-related morbidity

rows.label: Prevention
items: Minimize digital examinations after rupture; timely term-PROM induction; PPROM latency antibiotics when expectant

rows.label: Mimics
items: Epidural-associated fever: sterile inflammation possible; cannot dismiss coexisting infection
★ Postpartum endometritis: fever and fundal tenderness after birth → **clindamycin + gentamicin**
Pyelonephritis: flank tenderness and positive urine culture

intra-amniotic-infection.evidence: Diagnostic update checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG 2024](https://doi.org/10.1097/aog.0000000000005593); management follows established ACOG teaching.

menopause.name: Menopause
menopause.scope: Perimenopause, menopause transition, vasomotor symptoms, genitourinary syndrome of menopause, HRT
menopause.core: Menopause is 12 months without menses from ovarian follicle depletion; manage bothersome symptoms according to uterine status and hormone-treatment risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Natural transition typically in late 40s–50s; smoking, oophorectomy, chemotherapy or pelvic radiation accelerate onset
Menopause before 40 suggests primary ovarian insufficiency and requires a separate evaluation

rows.label: Clues
items: Perimenopause: cycle variability and skipped periods; fertility remains possible
Vasomotor episodes: abrupt heat, flushing, sweating, disturbed sleep; mood symptoms can coexist
Genitourinary syndrome: dryness, dyspareunia, urinary urgency and recurrent UTIs; pale thin mucosa

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ↓Follicles → ↓estradiol/inhibin and ↑FSH; hypothalamic thermoregulatory changes drive hot flashes
Urogenital estrogen deficiency thins epithelium, raises vaginal pH and changes flora

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical symptoms at **≥45 years → clinical diagnosis**; routine FSH unnecessary
Unexpected amenorrhea → pregnancy test; earlier menopause → FSH/estradiol and targeted thyroid/prolactin evaluation
Postmenopausal bleeding → endometrial evaluation; do not attribute to normal transition
Hormonal contraception alters bleeding/FSH interpretation; amenorrhea on contraception alone does not establish menopause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Bothersome hot flashes, low risk, generally <60 or within 10 years → **systemic estrogen**
★ Intact uterus → **add progestogen**; hysterectomy → estrogen alone usually sufficient
Avoid systemic hormones with unexplained bleeding, estrogen-sensitive cancer, prior VTE/stroke/MI or active liver disease
Hormones unsuitable → **venlafaxine, paroxetine or gabapentin**; selected fezolinetant requires liver monitoring
★ Isolated GSM → lubricants/moisturizers then **low-dose vaginal estrogen**; routine progestogen generally unnecessary

rows.label: Complications
items: Bone loss, fracture, sexual dysfunction; oral systemic estrogen increases VTE/stroke risk
Combined systemic hormones can increase breast cancer risk; unopposed uterine estrogen causes endometrial hyperplasia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Weight-bearing exercise, adequate calcium/vitamin D, smoking cessation; age/risk-based osteoporosis screening
Hormone treatment not for primary cardiovascular/dementia prevention; reassess symptoms and risks periodically
Continue contraception during transition until menopause criteria met; menopausal hormones do not prevent pregnancy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperthyroidism: persistent heat intolerance, tachycardia, suppressed TSH
Pregnancy: positive hCG despite irregular cycles

normal-and-abnormal-labor.name: Normal and abnormal labor
normal-and-abnormal-labor.scope: Latent vs active first stage, second stage, active phase protraction and arrest (oxytocin, cesarean), false labor (Braxton Hicks), operative vaginal delivery, labor induction
normal-and-abnormal-labor.core: True labor produces progressive cervical change; dystocia management depends on stage, contraction adequacy, fetal status, and descent.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Nulliparity, obesity, fetal macrosomia, malposition, cephalopelvic disproportion, inadequate uterine contractions

rows.label: Clues
items: Assess membrane status, presentation, fetal heart tracing, serial dilation, station, and maternal vital signs
★ Tachysystole: **>5 contractions/10 minutes**, averaged over 30 minutes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dysfunctional powers, passenger, or passage → delayed dilation or descent

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Active arrest requires ruptured membranes: no change after **4 hours adequate** or 6 hours inadequate contractions
Adequate activity: ≥200 Montevideo units; intrauterine pressure catheter when external assessment insufficient
Prolonged pushing: >3 hours nulliparous, >2 hours multiparous; individualize by descent and fetal status
Failed induction requires ≥12–18 hours oxytocin after ROM; slow latent phase alone does not mandate cesarean

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Protraction with weak contractions → **oxytocin**, amniotomy; established active arrest → cesarean
Tachysystole → stop oxytocin, lateral positioning; persistent fetal compromise → terbutaline, expedited delivery
★ Operative vaginal birth requires full dilation, ruptured membranes, engaged head, known position, skilled operator
Unfavorable cervix → balloon or prostaglandin ripening, then oxytocin; avoid misoprostol after prior cesarean
Avoid vacuum before 34 weeks or with face presentation; failed operative attempt → cesarean

rows.label: Complications
items: Maternal infection, hemorrhage, exhaustion; neonatal hypoxia
Forceps/vacuum → maternal lacerations, neonatal scalp injury; vacuum → subgaleal hemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Induce for maternal/fetal indications or offer elective induction from 39 weeks; no elective earlier delivery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Braxton Hicks: irregular contractions without cervical change
Obstructed labor: adequate contractions without progress; augmentation cannot correct mechanical obstruction

ovarian-cysts.name: Ovarian cysts
ovarian-cysts.scope: Follicular cyst, corpus luteum cyst, theca lutein cyst (hyperstimulation), mature cystic teratoma (dermoid), unilocular vs multilocular, surveillance intervals, cystectomy indications, cyst rupture
ovarian-cysts.core: Most reproductive-age ovarian cysts are benign; morphology, symptoms, menopausal status, and persistence determine observation versus surgery.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Ovulatory cycles, early pregnancy; ovulation induction or markedly elevated hCG → bilateral ovarian enlargement
Postmenopausal adnexal masses carry higher malignancy risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Incidental mass, pelvic pressure, unilateral discomfort; sudden pain after intercourse/exertion suggests rupture
★ Sudden severe pain with vomiting → **torsion**; syncope/hypotension → major intraperitoneal bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Functional lesions arise during ovulation; dermoids contain differentiated germ-cell tissues

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Pregnancy test first; **transvaginal ultrasound** characterizes wall, septations, solid elements, flow, free fluid
Simple unilocular: thin wall, anechoic, no solid vascular component; multiloculation warrants closer characterization
Papillary/solid vascular components, thick septa, ascites → malignancy evaluation; CA-125 nonspecific premenopausally
Normal Doppler flow does not exclude torsion; urgent clinical concern overrides reassuring imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Stable presumed hemorrhagic cyst → analgesia; uncertain resolution → repeat ultrasound in **6–12 weeks**
Asymptomatic simple cyst: follow-up generally above 5–7 cm premenopause, 3–5 cm postmenopause
Confidently simple surveilled cyst → ultrasound around 6–12 months; shorter interval if characterization uncertain
★ Hemodynamic instability → IV fluids/blood and urgent laparoscopy; torsion → detorsion with ovarian preservation
Persistent/enlarging, symptomatic, large, suspicious mass → surgery/referral; OCPs do not shrink existing cysts

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemoperitoneum, ovarian infarction, reduced ovarian reserve after surgery

rows.label: Prevention
items: Ovulation suppression may reduce new functional cyst formation; counsel urgent reassessment for acute pain

rows.label: Mimics
items: Ectopic pregnancy: positive hCG with pregnancy outside uterus
Tubo-ovarian abscess: fever, cervical motion tenderness, inflammatory complex mass

table.title: Cyst identities
rows: Thick crenulated wall; hemorrhage, peripheral vascularity
Bilateral multicystic ovaries; regress as hCG falls

ovarian-cysts.evidence: Simple-cyst thresholds checked 2026-10-30: [SRU 2019 consensus](https://pubs.rsna.org/doi/10.1148/radiol.2019191354); acute management established teaching.

physician-patient-communication.name: Physician-patient communication
physician-patient-communication.scope: Medical interpreters, limited English proficiency, delivering bad news, empathetic communication, family requests to withhold information
physician-patient-communication.core: Respect autonomy through understandable, honest, empathic dialogue; identify what patients understand and want before sharing decisions or sensitive information.

rows.label: Principle
items: Confidentiality, cultural humility, informed choice; language barriers never imply impaired capacity
Patient preferences determine family involvement and desired level of disclosure

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Qualified medical interpreter**, free to patient; speak directly to patient in short segments
★ Bad news: privacy → understanding/preferences → warning → plain disclosure → empathy → plan
Validate emotion; open questions, silence, teach-back; explore beliefs before correcting misinformation

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid jargon, false reassurance, interrupting, arguing, blaming, or premature advice
Avoid routine reliance on children/family for interpreting consent or sensitive discussions
Avoid promising cure or confidentiality beyond legal limits

rows.label: Exceptions
items: ★ **Family requests nondisclosure → ask patient privately**; patient preferences control disclosure
Capable patient may decline details or designate another recipient; document preference
Emergency without interpreter → temporary available help while securing qualified interpretation

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Therapeutic privilege is narrow**; anticipated distress alone never justifies withholding diagnosis
Anger → acknowledge concern, clarify cause, establish boundaries if threatening; no reflex discharge
Requested adult-family interpreter → verify suitability/privacy/voluntariness; offer professional

physician-patient-communication.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [HHS interpreter guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/civil-rights/for-individuals/faqs/may-an-lep-person-use-a-family-member-as-an-interpreter/index.html); established autonomy and bad-news communication principles.

polycystic-ovary-syndrome.name: Polycystic ovary syndrome
polycystic-ovary-syndrome.scope: Rotterdam criteria (hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, polycystic ovaries), metabolic risks, weight loss, oral contraceptives, ovulation induction (letrozole, clomiphene)
polycystic-ovary-syndrome.core: Hyperandrogenism and chronic ovulatory dysfunction after exclusion of alternative causes suggest PCOS; management follows metabolic, menstrual and fertility priorities.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, insulin resistance and obesity; lean patients can also have PCOS
Pubertal transition can mimic disease, requiring stricter adolescent diagnostic criteria

rows.label: Clues
items: Irregular/infrequent menses, infertility, hirsutism, acne or androgenic alopecia
Acanthosis nigricans suggests hyperinsulinemia; obesity is supportive, not required
Rapid virilization, deep voice or markedly elevated androgens → investigate tumor rather than assume PCOS

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insulin resistance and ovarian androgen excess impair follicular maturation and ovulation
Absent cyclic progesterone permits persistent estrogen-driven endometrial proliferation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Adults: **2 of 3 Rotterdam** features—hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, polycystic ovarian morphology
Exclude mimics: **hCG, TSH, prolactin, morning 17-hydroxyprogesterone**; latter screens nonclassic CAH
Total/free testosterone for biochemical androgen assessment; DHEAS if adrenal source suspected
★ Irregular cycles plus hyperandrogenism → **ultrasound not required**; LH:FSH ratio not diagnostic
BP, lipid profile and **oral glucose tolerance test** assess metabolic risk; adolescent diagnosis avoids ultrasound criteria

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Lifestyle/weight management for all; modest weight loss can restore ovulation in overweight patients
★ No pregnancy desired → **combined OCP** for cycles/androgen symptoms; cyclic progestin or LNG-IUD protects endometrium
Persistent hirsutism → spironolactone with reliable contraception; allow months for hair response
Metabolic risk/insulin resistance → metformin; less effective than OCP for androgen symptoms
★ Anovulatory infertility → **letrozole first-line**; clomiphene alternative after evaluating other infertility factors

rows.label: Complications
items: Endometrial hyperplasia/cancer, infertility, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, OSA and depression
Pregnancy → increased gestational diabetes and hypertensive-disorder risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: Regular progestin exposure for prolonged amenorrhea; persistent abnormal bleeding → endometrial assessment
Periodic glycemic/BP/lipid reassessment; preconception metabolic optimization and folate

rows.label: Mimics
items: Androgen-secreting tumor: rapid progression, severe virilization
Nonclassic CAH: elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone
Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea: low estrogen with exercise/energy deficit

postpartum-care.name: Postpartum care
postpartum-care.scope: Normal puerperal changes, lochia, uterine involution, perineal and cesarean wound healing, breastfeeding, postpartum depression screening, routine postpartum visit
postpartum-care.core: Postpartum care is an ongoing assessment of recovery, mood, infant feeding, contraception, and chronic disease after every birth.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ All postpartum patients; assess support, sleep, safety, sexual health, and reproductive goals

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Contact within **3 weeks**; comprehensive visit by **12 weeks**, with earlier risk-based review
Hypertensive disorder → BP within 7–10 days; severe hypertension → within 72 hours

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Edinburgh or PHQ-9 depression screen; assess suicidality directly after positive self-harm response
BP, bleeding, fundal tenderness; inspect perineum/incision for erythema, drainage, separation
Observe latch/milk transfer; frequent feeds, lactation support; cracked nipples → correct positioning

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Heavy bleeding, fever, dyspnea, severe headache → urgent evaluation
Mood screen positive → diagnostic interview, psychotherapy/SSRI; psychosis → emergency hospitalization
Increasing wound pain/purulence → evaluate infection; breast fluctuance → ultrasound for abscess

rows.label: Traps
items: Ovulation may precede first period; discuss contraception before discharge
Lactational contraception: amenorrhea, exclusive frequent breastfeeding, infant <6 months
Postpartum hypertension and cardiomyopathy can first appear after discharge

table.title: Expected recovery
rows: Descends daily; near prepregnancy size by 6 weeks
Pain progressively improves; keep clean, monitor healing
Early cramping and fluid loss; breastfeeding intensifies cramping

postpartum-care.evidence: Visit timing checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG postpartum care](https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/05/optimizing-postpartum-care); normal physiology established teaching.

postpartum-hemorrhage.name: Postpartum hemorrhage
postpartum-hemorrhage.scope: Primary postpartum hemorrhage (uterine atony, lacerations, retained placenta, coagulopathy), secondary postpartum hemorrhage (retained products of conception, endometritis), barrier methods, surgical management
postpartum-hemorrhage.core: Excessive bleeding after delivery demands simultaneous resuscitation and cause-directed control: Tone, Trauma, Tissue and Thrombin.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Uterine overdistention, prolonged/augmented labor, chorioamnionitis, magnesium, prior PPH → atony
Operative delivery → trauma; placenta accreta/retention → tissue; abruption/sepsis → coagulopathy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Boggy enlarged uterus** → atony; firm uterus with bleeding → laceration or other cause
Incomplete placenta → retained tissue; diffuse oozing → coagulopathy
Shock out of proportion to visible loss → concealed hematoma or inversion
Delayed bleeding >24 hours to weeks postpartum → retained products, endometritis or subinvolution

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Myometrial contraction compresses placental-bed vessels; failed contraction or disrupted tissue prevents hemostasis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Quantify blood loss; US definition **≥1000 mL or hypovolemia within 24 hours**, regardless of route
WHO 2025 earlier treatment trigger: ≥500 mL, or ≥300 mL with abnormal hemodynamic signs
Assess uterine tone, inspect birth canal/placenta; CBC, coagulation studies, fibrinogen and crossmatch
Ultrasound for suspected retained products; avoid delaying control in active unstable bleeding

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Hemorrhage team, two large IVs, warmed balanced blood resuscitation; massage, empty bladder, **oxytocin**
★ **Tranexamic acid within 3 hours** alongside first-response treatment
Refractory atony → **balloon/vacuum**, embolization if stable; compression sutures/arterial ligation or hysterectomy
Laceration → repair; retained tissue → evacuation; inversion → manual replacement before uterotonics
Endometritis → **clindamycin + gentamicin**

rows.label: Complications
items: DIC, AKI, shock, death; severe ischemia → Sheehan syndrome
Transfusion complications and hysterectomy-related fertility loss; delayed anemia impairs recovery

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prophylactic **oxytocin after delivery**, active third-stage management and antenatal anemia treatment
Risk assessment, blood availability and team readiness; routine prophylactic TXA not recommended for vaginal birth

rows.label: Mimics
items: Amniotic fluid embolism: sudden hypoxia/collapse with DIC
Pulmonary embolism: hypoxia/chest pain without primary uterine blood loss

preterm-labor.name: Preterm labor
preterm-labor.scope: Preterm labor (<37 weeks), cervical insufficiency, tocolysis (indomethacin, nifedipine), antenatal corticosteroids (betamethasone), magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection, GBS chemoprophylaxis
preterm-labor.core: Regular contractions with cervical change before 37 weeks; briefly delay eligible early births to improve neonatal outcomes, without prolonging unsafe pregnancies.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior spontaneous preterm birth, short cervix, multiple gestation, infection, smoking, uterine anomalies
Cervical surgery or prior painless second-trimester loss suggests cervical insufficiency

rows.label: Clues
items: Pelvic pressure, backache, increased discharge, contractions; assess membrane rupture and bleeding
Fever, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia → intraamniotic infection; maternal/fetal instability changes delivery timing

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Premature inflammatory/uterine activation versus mechanically weak cervix with painless dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Sterile speculum examination** for pooling and cervix; ultrasound dates pregnancy and assesses presentation
Transvaginal cervical length; selected symptomatic cases: negative fetal fibronectin predicts low imminent birth risk
Collect GBS culture, urine studies; exclude previa before digital examination with bleeding

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Birth within 7 days, **24–33 6/7 weeks** → betamethasone; selected untreated 34–36 6/7-week pregnancies also eligible
★ Delivery expected <32 weeks → **magnesium sulfate** for neuroprotection, not primary tocolysis
Tocolysis: 48 hours for steroids/transfer; no maintenance; late-preterm steroids avoided with pregestational diabetes
★ **No tocolysis** with infection, significant abruption, severe preeclampsia, or fetal compromise; proceed toward delivery
Intrapartum penicillin for positive/unknown GBS; no routine antibiotics for intact membranes without infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Neonatal RDS, IVH, NEC, sepsis, cerebral palsy; magnesium toxicity → hyporeflexia, respiratory depression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Singleton short cervix ≤20 mm before 24 weeks → vaginal progesterone; consider at 21–25 mm
Cervical insufficiency/prior qualifying loss → cerclage; selected prior preterm birth plus short cervix also eligible
17-hydroxyprogesterone caproate no longer recommended; progesterone without short cervix does not prevent recurrence

rows.label: Mimics
items: Braxton Hicks: no progressive dilation
Cervical insufficiency: painless dilation, minimal contractions
PPROM: membrane rupture precedes labor; distinct latency-antibiotic pathway

pubertal-development.name: Pubertal development
pubertal-development.scope: Tanner stages, normal thelarche vs breast mass, premature adrenarche, precocious puberty, constitutional delay of growth and puberty
pubertal-development.core: Interpret sexual maturation by sequence, age, growth velocity, and bone age; isolated benign variants lack progressive gonadal activation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Constitutional delay often familial; chronic illness, undernutrition, excess exercise delay maturation
CNS lesions, gonadal/adrenal hormone excess, exogenous sex steroids can cause early puberty

rows.label: Clues
items: Girls: breast budding precedes peak growth, then menarche about 2–3 years later
Boys: testes enlarge before penile growth; pubic hair reflects adrenarche, not necessarily gonadarche
★ Asymmetric tender **subareolar breast bud** at expected age usually normal; hard eccentric mass needs evaluation
Rapid height acceleration, advancing secondary characteristics, neurologic symptoms → pathologic early maturation concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Central puberty: hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility → LH/FSH → gonadal steroids
Adrenarche produces adrenal androgens independently; peripheral hormone excess suppresses pituitary gonadotropins

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Precocious: secondary sexual development **before 8 years girls or 9 years boys**
★ Delayed: **no breasts by 13**, no testes ≥4 mL by 14; evaluate absent menarche by 15
Growth chart, Tanner examination, bone age; LH/FSH, estradiol/testosterone, TSH selected by pattern
Central precocity → pubertal basal/stimulated LH; brain MRI especially boys, young girls, neurologic signs
Peripheral pattern → targeted adrenal/gonadal tests/imaging; isolated adrenarche requires exclusion of rapid virilization

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Progressive central precocity → **GnRH agonist**; treat CNS cause when present
Peripheral precocity → remove hormone source or treat tumor/adrenal disorder; GnRH agonist alone ineffective
Constitutional delay → reassurance, follow growth; distress → specialist-guided brief sex-steroid course
Benign premature thelarche/adrenarche → observe progression; no automatic hormonal treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Early epiphyseal closure → reduced adult height; psychosocial distress
Missed hypogonadism → impaired bone accrual; untreated CNS/tumor cause may progress

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate nutrition, manage chronic disease, avoid household hormone exposure; serial growth surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary gonadal failure: high LH/FSH, low sex steroids
Permanent central hypogonadism: absent progression rather than eventual familial catch-up

pubertal-development.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric endocrine timing and Tanner staging.

rh-alloimmunization.name: Rh alloimmunization
rh-alloimmunization.scope: Rh(D) and other red cell alloimmunization (Kell, Duffy), anti-D immune globulin prophylaxis, indirect Coombs titer monitoring, fetomaternal hemorrhage (Kleihauer-Betke), middle cerebral artery Doppler for fetal anemia
rh-alloimmunization.core: Maternal IgG against fetal red-cell antigens crosses the placenta, causing fetal anemia, hydrops, and neonatal hemolysis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Antigen-negative mother/positive fetus; prior pregnancy, transfusion, bleeding, trauma, invasive procedures
Anti-D, anti-Kell, and anti-Duffy clinically significant; ABO incompatibility usually milder

rows.label: Clues
items: Often asymptomatic mother; fetal ascites, skin edema, placentomegaly, cardiomegaly
Neonate: early jaundice, pallor, reticulocytosis; severe disease → cardiovascular collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: First exposure sensitizes; subsequent antigen exposure produces an anamnestic response
Kell antibodies additionally suppress erythropoiesis; low titers can still cause severe disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First prenatal visit: ABO/Rh type + **indirect Coombs**; repeat before routine antenatal prophylaxis
Identify antibody → fetal antigen status, serial titers; neonatal **direct Coombs** detects RBC-bound antibodies
★ Critical titer, often **1:16**, or previously affected pregnancy → middle cerebral artery Doppler
MCA peak systolic velocity >1.5 MoM → fetal blood sampling; Kell warrants specialist surveillance
Kleihauer-Betke quantifies hemorrhage for dosing: **300 µg covers 30 mL fetal whole blood**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe preterm fetal anemia → **intrauterine transfusion**; near term → delivery
Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia → phototherapy; severe hemolysis → exchange transfusion

rows.label: Complications
items: High-output heart failure, stillbirth, bilirubin encephalopathy, delayed neonatal anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Unsensitized Rh-negative mother: **anti-D immune globulin** at 28 weeks and within 72 hours postpartum
Postpartum prophylaxis only with Rh-positive/unknown infant; also after sensitizing events; adjust dose for hemorrhage
★ Established anti-D sensitization → prophylaxis ineffective; no equivalent prophylaxis for Kell/Duffy
ACOG 2024: routine Rh testing/prophylaxis may be forgone for abortion/loss before 12 weeks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Parvovirus: nonimmune hydrops with negative maternal antibody screen
ABO hemolysis: may affect first pregnancy; fetal hydrops uncommon

rh-alloimmunization.evidence: Prophylaxis checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG Rh guidance](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/the-rh-factor-how-it-can-affect-your-pregnancy), [2024 update](https://doi.org/10.1097/AOG.0000000000005733); remaining content established teaching.

routine-prenatal-care.name: Routine prenatal care and early pregnancy
routine-prenatal-care.scope: Pregnancy diagnosis (beta-hCG), initial prenatal assessment, routine first-trimester screening, aneuploidy screening
routine-prenatal-care.core: Confirm and date pregnancy, assess maternal risks, offer one aneuploidy-screening strategy or diagnostic testing, and arrange time-sensitive prenatal studies.

rows.label: Who
items: All pregnancies; review obstetric history, drugs, illness, substance use, violence, family history
Offer carrier screening and genetic counseling; discuss patient preferences and right to decline

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Early visit: urine hCG confirms pregnancy; serum quantitative hCG for uncertain/complicated cases
★ First-trimester **ultrasound crown–rump length** best establishes gestational age
Serum screen 10–13 6/7 weeks; NT 11–13 6/7; cfDNA from 10 weeks

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Initial **CBC, ABO/Rh, antibody screen, urine culture**; HIV, syphilis, HBsAg, HCV, rubella immunity
GC/chlamydia by age/risk; offer one aneuploidy strategy regardless of maternal age
Anatomy ultrasound 18–22 weeks; AFP for open neural tube defects when not otherwise assessed

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Abnormal screen → counseling, ultrasound, **CVS/amniocentesis** before irreversible decisions
CVS: 10–13 weeks; amniocentesis: ≥15 weeks; neither automatically required after negative screening
Rh-negative, unsensitized → anti-D prophylaxis at 28 weeks and after sensitizing events

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **cfDNA is screening**, not diagnostic; does not screen open neural tube defects
Single hCG value cannot establish viability or location; pain/bleeding → ectopic evaluation
Folate before conception/early gestation; avoid alcohol, tobacco, teratogens; no live vaccines

sexual-assault.name: Sexual assault
sexual-assault.scope: Forensic examination, STI prophylaxis (ceftriaxone, doxycycline, metronidazole), HIV post-exposure prophylaxis, hepatitis B vaccination, emergency contraception, psychological counseling
sexual-assault.core: Trauma-informed care restores control: obtain separate consent for treatment, examination, evidence collection, and disclosure; prioritize immediate safety.

rows.label: Principle
items: Nonjudgmental language; explain each step, offer advocate/chaperone, permit stopping at any point

rows.label: Do
items: ★ Stabilize; offer **SANE exam**, preserve chain of custody; avoid treatment delay
Pregnancy test; site-specific STI NAAT; baseline HIV, HBV, syphilis serology

rows.label: Prophylaxis
items: ★ Adolescent/adult females: **ceftriaxone once + doxycycline/metronidazole for 7 days**
★ HIV substantial-risk exposure **≤72 hours** → 28-day PEP; never await source testing
Preferred PEP: **bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide**; check renal function/interactions

rows.label: Don't
items: Require police reporting, blame survivor, coerce examination, or promise absolute confidentiality

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Child/vulnerable-adult abuse, certain injuries → mandatory reporting; explain confidentiality limits
Prepubertal children → specialist testing; routine empiric STI prophylaxis generally deferred

rows.label: Follow-up
items: Results within 1 week; repeat HIV/syphilis tests, finish vaccines, arrange trauma-focused counseling
Ongoing danger/suicidality → urgent safety intervention; support survivor-directed reporting decisions

rows.label: Traps
items: Normal examination does not exclude assault; absent resistance or intoxication does not establish consent
Offer evidence collection despite bathing, clothing changes, or delayed presentation
Pregnancy → replace doxycycline with pregnancy-compatible chlamydia treatment, e.g., azithromycin

table.title: Additional prevention
rows: Offer ulipristal, levonorgestrel, or copper IUD

skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.name: Skin and soft tissue infections
skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.scope: Cellulitis, erysipelas, folliculitis, furuncles, carbuncles, lymphangitis, necrotizing fasciitis
skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.core: Skin infection management depends on purulence, systemic illness, and signs of deep tissue destruction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Skin breaks, tinea pedis, edema/lymphedema, diabetes, obesity, injection drug use
Prior MRSA, crowding, recent hospitalization; surgery or penetrating trauma raises deep-infection risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Warmth, tenderness, erythema; rapidly expanding margins or systemic toxicity require urgent reassessment
★ **Pain out of proportion**, bullae, anesthesia, crepitus, shock → necrotizing infection
Perineal involvement → Fournier gangrene; saltwater exposure → Vibrio, freshwater → Aeromonas

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Nonpurulent infection usually streptococcal; purulent lesions usually S aureus
Fascial spread and toxin-mediated injury → thrombosis, necrosis, sepsis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical diagnosis; **bedside ultrasound** if occult fluid collection suspected
Culture drained pus for severe, recurrent, or resistant infection; blood cultures for systemic toxicity
Suspected necrotizing disease → immediate surgical evaluation; imaging must not delay exploration
Low laboratory risk score or absent gas does not exclude necrotizing fasciitis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Deep infection → **urgent debridement + vancomycin + piperacillin-tazobactam**, add clindamycin for toxin suppression
Confirmed group A streptococcal necrotizing infection → penicillin + clindamycin
Severe cellulitis/systemic illness → IV cefazolin; MRSA risk → vancomycin
★ Abscess: add **antibiotics** for systemic signs, immunocompromise, extensive disease, or failed drainage

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, osteomyelitis, septic thrombophlebitis; tissue loss and amputation
Toxic shock, multiorgan failure; recurrent cellulitis worsens lymphatic dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat interdigital fungal infection, manage edema, skin hygiene, protect wounds
Recurrent staphylococcal infections → consider nasal mupirocin + chlorhexidine decolonization; avoid shared razors

rows.label: Mimics
items: Stasis dermatitis: chronic, often bilateral, itchy
DVT: deep swelling without superficial spreading infection; contact dermatitis: pruritic exposure-pattern rash

table.title: Superficial patterns
rows: Incision and drainage; TMP-SMX if needed

skin-and-soft-tissue-infections.evidence: Not checked online; established IDSA-based infection management.

syphilis.name: Syphilis
syphilis.scope: Primary syphilis, secondary syphilis, latent syphilis, tertiary syphilis, neurosyphilis, serologic testing, Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction, penicillin therapy
syphilis.core: Treponema pallidum infection progresses through mucocutaneous, asymptomatic, and destructive stages; neurologic, ocular, or auditory disease can occur anytime.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Unprotected sex, multiple partners, HIV; transplacental transmission during pregnancy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Primary: **painless chancre** with regional lymphadenopathy
Secondary: palms/soles rash, condylomata lata, generalized nodes, patchy alopecia
Tertiary: gummas, ascending aortic aneurysm; tabes dorsalis or dementia
Latent: reactive serology without symptoms; early = acquired within 1 year

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Spirochete dissemination → endarteritis; posterior column injury → sensory ataxia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RPR/VDRL + treponemal assay**; discordant reverse screen → second treponemal assay
Early chancre with negative serology → lesion testing or repeat serology
★ Neurologic deficits → **LP**; CSF-VDRL specific, negative result does not exclude
Quantitative RPR: early disease follow-up at 6/12 months; latent at 6/12/24 months
Tertiary disease → CSF assessment before treatment; isolated ocular/otic disease may not require LP

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pregnancy with penicillin allergy → **desensitization**, then stage-specific penicillin
Nonpregnant penicillin allergy, uncomplicated early infection → doxycycline for 14 days

rows.label: Complications
items: Jarisch-Herxheimer: fever/myalgias within 24 hours after treatment; supportive care, not allergy
Congenital infection → stillbirth, hearing loss, dental/bone abnormalities

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Partners exposed within **90 days** → presumptive early-syphilis treatment despite negative tests
HIV testing; prenatal screening; serial RPR after treatment, fourfold rise suggests reinfection/failure

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chancroid: painful ulcer, tender suppurative nodes
HSV: painful grouped vesicles; pityriasis rosea: herald patch, usually spares palms
Autoimmune false-positive RPR: negative confirmatory treponemal assay

syphilis.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [CDC STI guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/std/treatment-guidelines/syphilis.htm), including linked stage-specific guidance.

teratogens.name: Teratogens
teratogens.scope: Valproate and carbamazepine (neural tube defects), ACE inhibitors, isotretinoin, lithium (Ebstein anomaly), warfarin, alcohol (fetal alcohol syndrome), high-dose folic acid supplementation
teratogens.core: Exposure timing and agent determine fetal harm; review medications before conception and substitute safer treatments while preserving maternal disease control.

rows.label: Use
items: Preconception counseling, exposure assessment, and selection of pregnancy-compatible drugs

rows.label: Mechanism
items: Weeks 3–8 postconception: organogenesis → malformations; later exposure → growth/functional injury

rows.label: Adverse
items: ★ **Alcohol**: poor growth/development, smooth philtrum, thin upper lip, short palpebral fissures

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ **Isotretinoin contraindicated**; pregnancy testing and effective contraception required
Valproate generally avoided when alternatives effective; do not abruptly stop antiseizure drugs
ACE inhibitor → labetalol/nifedipine for pregnancy hypertension; warfarin usually → LMWH

rows.label: Monitor
items: ★ Prior NTD pregnancy → **folic acid 4 mg/day**, preconception through first trimester
Antiseizure exposure: folate **≥0.4 mg/day**; optimal higher dose uncertain, individualize
Lithium: levels, renal/thyroid tests; early exposure → detailed fetal cardiac assessment

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ No safe alcohol threshold; exposure alone does not mandate pregnancy termination
Mechanical heart valves may require individualized warfarin decisions despite fetal risks
Folate lowers NTD risk but does not erase valproate-associated malformations or developmental harm

table.title: Agent → characteristic fetal injury
rows: Neural tube defects; valproate neurodevelopmental toxicity
Fetal renal injury, oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia
Increased cardiac malformation risk, including Ebstein anomaly
Nasal hypoplasia, stippled epiphyses, fetal bleeding

teratogens.evidence: Folate checked 2026-10-30: [CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/folic-acid/hcp/clinical-overview/), [AAN/AES/SMFM 2024](https://www.aan.com/PressRoom/Home/PressRelease/5170); exposure patterns established pharmacology.

urinary-incontinence.name: Urinary incontinence
urinary-incontinence.core: Involuntary urine leakage is classified by triggers, urgency, bladder emptying, and ability to reach a toilet; reversible contributors often coexist.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childbirth, pelvic surgery, aging, obesity; diabetes, neurologic disease, prostate enlargement
Diuretics, sedatives, anticholinergics, constipation, infection, impaired mobility/cognition worsen control

rows.label: Clues
items: History: timing, volume, dysuria, weak stream, nocturia, fluid intake, obstetric/surgical and neurologic history
★ **New saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, retention** → urgent cauda equina evaluation
Continuous leakage after pelvic surgery suggests fistula; recurrent UTIs/hematuria require further investigation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Urethral support/sphincter failure, involuntary detrusor contraction, or impaired emptying produce distinct leakage patterns
Functional impairment can prevent continence despite intact lower urinary tract function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + voiding diary**, focused pelvic/prostate and neurologic examination; review medications
Cough stress test with reasonably full bladder; assess prolapse, atrophy, fecal impaction
★ Suspected retention/emptying symptoms → **postvoid residual**; persistent >200 mL suggests inadequate emptying
No routine initial urodynamics/cystoscopy; uncertainty, hematuria, refractory symptoms → additional testing

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat reversible contributor; mixed incontinence → target most bothersome component
★ **Pelvic floor training/bladder training** underpin conservative care; weight loss, reduce caffeine, timed voiding
Urgency drugs: mirabegron or antimuscarinic; discuss cognitive risk and avoid antimuscarinics with retention
Mirabegron may increase BP; avoid severe uncontrolled hypertension; refractory urgency → botulinum toxin or neuromodulation
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause → local vaginal estrogen when suitable; not systemic estrogen for leakage

rows.label: Complications
items: Dermatitis, falls from rushing, social isolation, sleep disruption
Overflow → hydronephrosis/renal injury; bladder botulinum toxin → retention, UTI

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, accessible toilet, mobility aids; bowel regularity, maintain strength and weight

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polyuria: high urine volume from hyperglycemia/diuresis rather than primary storage failure
Vaginal fistula: constant leakage unrelated to voiding urge or exertion

vaginitis.name: Vaginitis
vaginitis.scope: Bacterial vaginosis, Trichomoniasis, Vulvovaginal candidiasis, atrophic vaginitis, genitourinary syndrome of menopause
vaginitis.core: Vaginal discharge or irritation requires distinction among dysbiosis, sexually transmitted protozoal infection, yeast overgrowth, and hypoestrogenic mucosal change.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: BV: new partners, douching; trichomoniasis: sexual exposure
Candida: antibiotics, pregnancy, diabetes, immunosuppression; atrophy: menopause or other hypoestrogenic states

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus, dysuria, dyspareunia; discharge appearance overlaps, so symptoms alone insufficient
★ **Fever, lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness** → evaluate PID rather than isolated vaginitis
Postmenopausal bleeding needs assessment beyond assuming atrophy

rows.label: Pathophys
items: BV: lactobacilli depleted, anaerobes expand; Candida causes inflammatory overgrowth; Trichomonas is sexually transmitted
Low estrogen thins epithelium and reduces lactobacilli → mucosal fragility and elevated vaginal pH

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Vaginal pH, saline/KOH microscopy**, history and examination; NAAT improves infectious diagnosis
BV: ≥3 Amsel findings—typical discharge, pH elevation, clue cells, positive amine odor
★ Suspected trichomoniasis + negative wet mount → **NAAT**, not reassurance
Recurrent/complicated Candida → culture or PCR for species; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **oral metronidazole 7 days in women**; treat partners, abstain until completed/resolved
BV → oral metronidazole 7 days or vaginal metronidazole/clindamycin; treat symptomatic pregnancy
Candida → topical azole or oral fluconazole; **pregnancy: topical azole 7 days**, avoid oral fluconazole
GSM → moisturizers/lubricants, then low-dose vaginal estrogen for persistent symptoms; assess contraindication context
Recurrent BV: ACOG 2025 considers male-partner metronidazole + topical clindamycin; older boards omit

rows.label: Complications
items: BV/trichomoniasis associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and increased STI acquisition
Recurrent symptoms → reassess diagnosis, adherence, reinfection, diabetes or resistant/non-albicans yeast

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **retest women at about 3 months**; condoms, partner management
Avoid douching/irritants; no routine partner treatment for uncomplicated Candida

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: endocervical mucopus, friability, positive GC/CT NAAT
Contact dermatitis: external irritation after product exposure, no infectious findings

venous-thromboembolism.name: Venous thromboembolism
venous-thromboembolism.core: Unilateral swollen leg or sudden unexplained dyspnea with pleuritic pain; pulmonary embolism severity determined by hemodynamics, not clot size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobilization, surgery, malignancy, estrogen, pregnancy/postpartum, previous VTE, inherited thrombophilia

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT: asymmetric calf tenderness, warmth; PE: tachycardia, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, sometimes normal oxygen saturation
Syncope, elevated JVP, cool extremities → impending RV failure; normal chest radiograph does not exclude PE

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis/endothelial injury/hypercoagulability → venous clot; pulmonary obstruction → V/Q mismatch, RV pressure overload

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Wells/pretest probability** first; very low-risk + PERC-negative → no testing
★ Low/intermediate probability → **D-dimer**; negative excludes; positive/high probability → **CT pulmonary angiography**
Age >50: D-dimer threshold age × 10 ng/mL FEU; contrast contraindication → V/Q scan
DVT → compression US; negative proximal scan + persistent suspicion → repeat in 1 week

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Oxygen/support circulation; unstable and unsafe for CT → bedside **echo**; high suspicion/delayed imaging → anticoagulate
★ Most stable VTE → **apixaban/rivaroxaban**; pregnancy → LMWH; severe renal failure → UFH
Lysis contraindicated/fails → catheter thrombectomy/surgical embolectomy; active intracranial bleeding precludes lysis
Acute proximal DVT/PE + absolute anticoagulation contraindication → temporary **IVC filter**, remove when feasible

rows.label: Complications
items: Postthrombotic syndrome; persistent dyspnea → evaluate chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis → bleeding; heparin → HIT

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Major transient trigger → **3 months** anticoagulation; unprovoked/persistent risk → extended course if low bleeding risk
Hospital prophylaxis: LMWH; active bleeding → intermittent pneumatic compression; early mobilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: predominantly skin erythema, portal of entry
Ruptured Baker cyst: posterior knee symptoms, cyst on US
Pneumonia: focal infiltrate and infectious prodrome

table.title: Treatment branches; 2026 PE guidance uses categories A–E
rows: Stable; low PESI/sPESI; no RV injury
Normotensive + RV dysfunction and/or troponin elevation
Sustained SBP <90 mm Hg or shock

vulvar-cancer.name: Vulvar cancer
vulvar-cancer.scope: Squamous cell carcinoma, melanoma of the vulva, lichen sclerosus malignant transformation, vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia (VIN), Paget disease of the vulva, staging, wide local excision, sentinel node biopsy
vulvar-cancer.core: Persistent vulvar pruritus with a focal ulcer, plaque, or mass requires biopsy, especially in an older patient.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HPV-related disease: smoking, immunosuppression; HPV-independent disease: older age, lichen sclerosus
Prior vulvar HSIL/VIN; chronic symptoms repeatedly treated without tissue diagnosis delay detection

rows.label: Clues
items: Nonhealing lesion, bleeding, dyspareunia, focal pain; enlarged inguinal nodes suggest regional spread
★ **Changing pigmented lesion** requires melanoma evaluation; amelanotic lesions also occur

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Squamous carcinoma spreads locally, then to inguinofemoral nodes; nodal involvement strongly influences prognosis
HPV-associated HSIL and HPV-independent differentiated VIN are distinct precursor pathways

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Punch/incisional biopsy** of suspicious lesion; sample viable edge, not only necrotic center
Document lesion size, depth, focality, proximity to midline; examine groin nodes
Suspicious nodes → ultrasound-guided sampling; advanced local extent → pelvic MRI and metastatic imaging
Stage by stromal invasion, adjacent-organ extension, and nodal/distant spread; evaluate multifocal disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive disease → **wide local excision** with negative margins
Microinvasive SCC ≤1 mm stromal invasion generally needs no groin-node surgery
★ Unifocal **<4 cm**, invasion >1 mm, clinically negative nodes → sentinel-node biopsy
Larger/multifocal or node-positive disease → groin treatment; locally advanced → chemoradiation and/or surgery
Paget → excision; VIN → excision, or laser/imiquimod after excluding invasion

rows.label: Complications
items: Local recurrence, nodal metastasis; surgery/radiation → lymphedema, wound breakdown, sexual dysfunction

rows.label: Prevention
items: HPV vaccination, tobacco cessation; high-potency topical corticosteroids for lichen sclerosus, continued surveillance

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lichen simplex chronicus: diffuse scratch-induced thickening; biopsy persistent focal changes
Candidiasis: yeast on microscopy, responds to antifungal; persistent lesion still needs sampling

table.title: Histologic clues
rows: Ulcerated/keratotic mass; HPV or inflammatory pathway
Asymmetry, irregular color/border; Breslow depth guides management
Chronic eczematous red plaque; intraepithelial glandular cells

vulvar-cancer.evidence: Excision/node selection checked 2026-10-30: [NCI PDQ](https://www.cancer.gov/types/vulvar/hp/vulvar-treatment-pdq); remaining pathology established teaching.
